record.final_answer:
Yes — it will fail, not just be slow.

Corvane gateway 2.3 (docs.corvane.example/multipart, per my earlier reading) caps a multipart upload at 5000 parts, with parts 8 MiB–512 MiB. 8 MiB x 5000 caps an object at 39 GiB:

  60 GiB  = 61440 MiB / 8 MiB  = 7680 parts   -> over the limit

So the dump would upload for hours and then be rejected on the part count, wasting the whole night's transfer. 8 MiB was also the minimum allowed part size, which is why it worked back when the tarball was small.

Change: CHUNK_MB=8 -> 64. That is 960 parts at 60 GiB, and 64 MiB x 5000 covers growth to 312 GiB. 128 MiB would work too, but 64 is the sweet spot — still well under the 512 MiB max, and it keeps retries cheap on a flaky link.

I also added a fail-fast guard and a comment recording the limits, so the next growth spurt produces a clear error instead of a doomed upload:

  scripts/upload.sh
    CHUNK_MB=64
    MAX_PARTS=5000
    size=$(wc -c < "$file")
    ... parts = ceil(size/chunk); if parts > MAX_PARTS -> error "raise CHUNK_MB", exit 1

Verified with a stub corvane-cli and sparse files: 60 GiB and 300 GiB upload as 64MiB parts; 320 GiB stops with "needs 5120 parts ... over Corvane's 5000-part limit"; 0-byte and 8-byte files unaffected; syntax clean under sh and dash.

One thing blocks applying it: writes to /stand/ws are refused — HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT is set to /opt/data, so both write_file and patch were denied on /stand/ws/scripts/upload.sh (the tested copy lives in /tmp/hermes/cache/scratch/t/upload.sh). Unset that variable or add /stand/ws to it and I'll write the change in place. Also note corvane-cli isn't installed in this environment, so the real upload itself is untested — only the part-size arithmetic and the guard are.
